references.citation: Doumith M, Buchrieser C, Glaser P, Jacquet C, Martin P. Differentiation of the major Listeria monocytogenes serovars by multiplex PCR. J Clin Microbiol 2004;42(8):3819-22.
references.note: The five-marker multiplex (prs, lmo0737, lmo1118, ORF2819, ORF2110) the doumith_serogroup scheme encodes, including the grouping of serovars.

caveats: 4b, 4d and 4e share every published molecular marker in this panel; the call is the group, and separating them needs cgMLST or antisera.
EGD-e, the reference genome for 1/2a, types as IIc because it carries lmo1118 — documented in Doumith 2004, not a tool artefact.
prs is genus-level, not L. monocytogenes-specific: other Listeria species carry it, so prs alone never proves Lm. It gates the scheme as a control gene.

Horizontal transfer of the lineage-II lmo0737 cassette produces the IVb-v pattern in otherwise-4b strains (declared before IVb so the variant wins), and rare HGT of the ORF markers can fake a IIb profile.
Serogroup is not lineage, and neither is a virulence verdict: hypovirulent and non-cytotoxic Lm can carry any of these profiles.
